releases.title: Mobile App Release, automatic rebuilds and a signing key that lasts
releases.md:
## AS-IS

Everything from v1.0.0 to v1.6.0 is unchanged. Leads, clients and the service board, client deletion by OTP with its archive, the Super Admin company workspace and every one of its tabs, DPDP consent, the website builder, the per-company apps and their GitHub build, chat with its groups and notices, push notifications, per-company cron, retention, the shared cache and every earlier fix all behave exactly as they did. Nothing was removed.

Two things on that page were changed, both with your approval, and both are set out under *Updates / Modifications* below.

## New Features

- **The Mobile App tab no longer hangs.** It had no error handling at all: a single failed call left it spinning for ever with nothing on screen and no way to find out why. It now says what went wrong — including the status and the platform's own message — and offers **Try again**. The rest of the company page was never affected and still isn't.
- **Super Admin → Mobile App Release** is a new module. Every company's app in one place:
  - **Four counts across the top** — building now, ready and failed over the last seven days, and how many phones are on the newest version of *their own company's* app (each company has its own version line, so this is worked out per company and then added up).
  - **Start a build** for one company, or for **every company that already has an app**. A company with no app yet is deliberately skipped by the bulk action — its first build fixes the application id and the signing key, which is not something a bulk action should decide.
  - **Every build, across every company**, with filters for company, platform and status, what started it (by hand, on a push, or across every company), and a link to the run on GitHub. A running build refreshes itself until it finishes.
- **Automatic rebuilds on new code.** A push to the app's own repository rebuilds the app of every company that has *Auto build* on, each with its own name, icon, colours and address; phones get it as an ordinary update. There are two ways to connect it and both are in the panel: a step in the repository's workflow, or a repository webhook (`/api/public/webhooks/github/push`, content type JSON, "Just the push event"). Both are signed with **BUILD_TRIGGER_SECRET**, which the screen shows, copies and can replace. A push to any branch other than the one being watched is accepted and ignored, so a feature branch never rebuilds anyone's app.
- **The Build screen on each company** now shows, before the list of builds:
  - **Downloads** — one card per platform with the version that is actually live, its size, when it finished, its full S3 path and a download button.
  - **Android signing** — the key this company's app is signed with, in plain words, with the application id, the alias, the version it has applied from and the certificate fingerprint.
- **A signing key that lasts, kept by the platform.** The platform now makes **one permanent Android key per company** at that company's first Android build and signs every later build with it, so an update installs over the old app instead of being refused.

## Updates / Modifications

- **Signing keys — this reverses a decision made in v1.5.0, with your approval.** Until now keys lived only in the build repository's GitHub secrets and the platform never held one. The platform now makes and keeps a key per company. How it is protected:
  - the keystore and both passwords are **encrypted with AES-256-GCM** before they are written, under a new setting `MOBILE_SIGNING_SECRET`. The database on its own cannot sign anything.
  - the key is **never a workflow input**, because inputs are printed in the run's own log. The build asks for it over the same signed channel it reports its result on, only while it is still running, and shreds the file when it finishes.
  - nothing in the key ever reaches a browser. The screens only ever see the fingerprint.
  - **a repository that already has `ANDROID_*` secrets still works**: if the platform has no key for a company, the build falls back to the repository's own, exactly as before.
  - **one reinstall, once.** A phone holding an app built before the platform's key needs a single uninstall-and-reinstall; every update after that installs over it. The Build screen says so, per company, and only while it is actually true.
- **The Build section of Super Admin → Company → Mobile App was restructured**, as approved: Downloads, then Android signing, then the builds list. **The builds table itself is unchanged** and still sits underneath with its download, cancel and delete actions.
- **`MobileBuild` gained three fields** — `signedBy`, `signingFingerprint` and `trigger` — and an index on `status`+`createdAt` for the all-company list. Existing rows are untouched; an older build simply has no value in them.
- **New module `mobile_release`.** Like every new module it starts **switched off**: give *Mobile App Release* to the Super Admin roles that should have it, under Role Management.
- **New settings:**
  - `MOBILE_SIGNING_SECRET` — required before the platform can keep signing keys. Without it, nothing breaks: builds fall back to the repository's `ANDROID_*` secrets and the Build screen says so.
  - `APP_BASE_URL` is now also used for `PLATFORM_URL` on the set-up panel. It was already in use elsewhere.
  - The build workflow gained one input, `signing_url`, and one secret it already had, `MOBILE_BUILD_SECRET`, is now also used to collect the key.
- **The `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` signing step was rewritten.** It used to fail outright when `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64` was missing. It now takes the platform's key first, the repository's secrets second, and only fails when there is neither — with a message saying which of the two to set.
- One wording fix on the Build screen: "A Android build is running now" now reads "An Android build is running now."

## Next

v1.8.0 — store builds (Google Play and App Store upload from the same screen), a per-company build history page on the company side, and attachments in chat.

releases.title: Chat, push notifications and the scrolling notice
releases.md:
## AS-IS

Everything from v1.0.0 to v1.5.0 is unchanged. Leads, clients and the service board, client deletion by OTP with its archive, the Super Admin company workspace and all twelve of its tabs, DPDP consent, the website builder, the company apps and their GitHub build, per-company cron, retention, the shared cache and every earlier fix all behave exactly as they did. Nothing was removed or renamed.

## New Features

- **Chats** is a new module on the company side, at `/app/chats`, and a screen in each company's app. One-to-one and group conversations, with the message appearing for everyone the moment it is sent.
- **One-to-one.** Anyone in the company can be messaged by name. A pair of people can only ever have one conversation — the database enforces it — so a second "New chat" with the same person opens the one that already exists rather than splitting the history in two.
- **Groups.** Someone with *Chats › Groups* may create a group with a name, a line about what it is for, and the members. Members see it immediately, on the web and on their phone, and get a push. A group can be renamed, its membership changed, and a member may leave it; joining and leaving are written into the conversation itself so the history explains itself.
- **Nobody's contact details are shared.** A member is known to other members by **name and role only** — a phone number or an e-mail address never leaves the server in anything chat sends. That is written into the code (`publicMember` in `shared/chat.ts`), not a setting, so a group cannot be used to collect contact details.
- **Push notifications** to each company's own app, through Expo, which hands them to Google and Apple. A phone registers itself at sign-in and is forgotten at sign-out, so a shared phone stops receiving the previous person's messages. A token the device no longer holds is dropped automatically.
- **The scrolling notice.** *Chats › Notices* posts a line that scrolls across the top of every screen — on the web and in the app — in one of three tones, optionally also sent as a push, with an optional stop time. A person can hide a notice on their own device; the next one still shows. Tapping it on the phone stops the movement so a long notice can be read.
- **Messages are stored first and delivered second.** The reply to "send" is only returned once the message is saved, so a message is never lost because the real-time service, or a phone, could not be reached — at worst it arrives a few seconds later.
- **It works with no real-time service at all.** With none configured, every screen falls back to asking the platform every few seconds and nothing else changes; the header says which it is doing ("Messages arrive the moment they are sent" or "refresh every few seconds").
- **Unread counts, read receipts and "typing…"** on both the web and the app. A conversation never re-downloads itself: it asks only for what has arrived since the last message it holds.
- **Retention covers chat.** Two new rows on *Retention Policy*: **Chat messages**, which keep for ever unless a period is chosen — a conversation is a record, not a log — and **Dormant phones**, which are dropped after 180 days *measured from when the app was last opened*, not from when the phone was registered, so an active phone is never unregistered.
- Creating or changing a group and posting or stopping a notice are written to **Activity Logs** like every other action.

## Updates / Modifications

- **New module `chats`**, with sub-modules *Groups* and *Notices*. Like every new module it starts **switched off in every plan**: tick *Chats* on the plans that should have it, then give *Groups* and *Notices* to the roles that should administer them. Until it is ticked, nothing about chat appears for anyone — no menu entry, no app screen.
- **New collections in each company's database**: `chatthreads`, `chatmessages`, `pushdevices`, `announcements`. Nothing existing was altered.
- **`LogKindDef` gained an optional `dateField`** so a kind can age from a field other than when it was written. Only *Dormant phones* uses it; every existing kind keeps exactly the behaviour it had.
- **The app** (`mobile/`) gains the Chats list, a conversation screen, the notice banner and push registration, and three packages: `expo-notifications`, `expo-device` and `pusher-js`. The notification icon and tint follow the company's colour. **Existing installed apps keep working** — the chat screen only appears for a build that includes it, so rebuild each company's app from *Super Admin › Company › Mobile App* when you want chat on the phone.
- **New environment settings** (platform-wide, not per company):
  - `REALTIME_PROVIDER` — `pusher` (default when the Pusher keys are present) or `ably`.
  - `PUSHER_APP_ID`, `PUSHER_KEY`, `PUSHER_SECRET`, `PUSHER_CLUSTER` — the cluster defaults to `ap2` (Mumbai), the nearest one to India, which is what keeps a message under a few tens of milliseconds.
  - `ABLY_API_KEY` — only if you choose Ably instead.
  - Leave all of them empty and chat still works, by polling.
- Push needs no key on the platform: Expo's service holds the Google and Apple credentials, which are created with the app in *Mobile App*.

## Next

v1.7.0 — attachments in chat (photo and document, into the company's own S3 folder), a per-user mute, and in-app notifications for the rest of the `NOTIFY_KINDS` list.

releases.md:
## AS-IS

Everything from v1.0.0 to v1.4.0 is unchanged. The company workspace and its tabs, DPDP consent, the website builder, per-company cron and retention, the shared cache and every earlier fix behave exactly as they did.

## New Features

- **Each company gets its own Android app** (and iOS once signing is set up), built from one shared source in `mobile/`. A build carries that company's name, icon, colours, application id and its own address, so the app signs in to that company and nothing else.
- **Super Admin › Company › Mobile App** names and brands the app, takes a 1024×1024 icon, picks the platforms, and builds. Builds show Queued → Building → Ready with a link to the run on GitHub, the file size, who started it and how many times it was downloaded. A build can be cancelled or deleted, and **Your set-up now** lists every setting the build needs, green or red.
- **The build runs on GitHub Actions** (`.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`) in this repository, next to the app source. The signed file is uploaded to that company's own S3 folder under `<COMPANY CODE>/app/<platform>/<version>/`, and the result is reported back signed with `MOBILE_BUILD_SECRET` — so only a build the platform started can report one.
- **No signing key is ever held by the platform.** Android and iOS certificates live in the build repository's GitHub secrets. The Android build stops rather than signing with a throw-away key, because a throw-away key means staff must uninstall the app — losing whatever is held on the device — to take the next version.
- **The company downloads its app** from Settings › Mobile App: the newest ready build per platform, with its version, size and date.
- **The app.** Sign in with the same e-mail and password as the web; the **DPDP notice** at the first sign-in and whenever a new version is published, which must be scrolled to the end before it can be accepted (recorded with source "app"); then a hamburger menu with **Dashboard**, **Chats** (arriving in v1.6.0) and **Profile**, which carries sign out and the version with its build number.
- **What the app shows follows the platform, not the build.** The Mobile Modules tab and each user's role are read when the app starts, so changing either needs no rebuild. Only the name, icon, colours, application id or address do.
- **Knowledge Base › GitHub build** explains the whole set-up: the repository, the platform settings, making the Android keystore, the repository secrets, the first build and what each failure message means.
- Builds that never report back are marked failed by the nightly housekeeping job after 90 minutes, so a row never spins for ever.

## Updates / Modifications

- `Company` gained `mobile`; `MobileBuild` is a new collection in the main database.
- `/auth/me` now returns `mobileScreens` for a company user — the Mobile Modules list the app reads at start-up.
- A company-side **Mobile App** module appears under Settings. Like every new module it starts switched off in each plan: tick it on the plans that should have it.
- New environment setting: `MOBILE_BUILD_SECRET`. The same value must be a secret in the build repository. The rest of the `GITHUB_BUILD_*` and `MOBILE_*` settings documented in v1.3.1 are now read.

## Next

v1.6.0 — one-to-one and group chat in the apps with a managed real-time service, push notifications and the scrolling notice, and the admin side that creates groups and onboards users.

releases.title: DPDP consent and the company website
releases.md:
## AS-IS

Everything from v1.0.0 to v1.3.1 is unchanged. The company workspace and its tabs, per-company cron and retention, the shared-cache fix, client delete, Sales Order grouping, the Outstanding split and every earlier fix behave exactly as they did. Nothing was removed.

## New Features

### DPDP consent

- **The notice.** Each company has one consent notice, written here in Markdown or uploaded as a PDF or Word file. An upload's text is pulled out so the screen can show it as a page that scrolls — a browser's own PDF viewer cannot be watched, and reading before accepting is the point — while the original file is kept in the company's S3 folder and offered as a download beside it. Publishing creates a new version; earlier versions are kept, so an old acceptance always points at the exact text that was accepted.
- **One notice serves every company.** The platform keeps a default notice written with placeholders — `{{company.name}}`, `{{company.legalName}}`, `{{company.address}}`, the grievance officer and so on — which are filled in with each company's own details when it is shown. A company can use it as it is, edit it into its own, or upload its own, and go back to the platform's at any time.
- **The consent screen** at `<company address>/consent`: the notice, a progress bar, and an **Accept** button that stays off until the notice has been scrolled to the end and a sensible amount of time has passed. There is no Cancel — closing the window simply means nothing was accepted. The five purposes are listed separately: three are needed to answer an enquiry and keep lawful records, two (offers, analytics) are the person's to choose. Open it with `?from=app` or `?from=crm` to record where it came from, and `?next=/path` to send the person on once they accept.
- **Every acceptance is evidence.** Who accepted, when, which version, how long the notice was open, how far it was scrolled, when the end was reached, which purposes were ticked, from which page, with the IP and device. The same checks run again on the server, because a screen is only a screen.
- **Withdrawing** is recorded against the same row rather than deleting it — the Act requires the record itself to survive.
- **Cookie consent.** The website shows a banner with Strictly necessary (always on), Preferences, Analytics and Marketing. What each visitor chose is recorded and listed.
- **A new DPDP tab under Logs**, and a **DPDP** module under Settings, both permission-gated. Super Admin sees the same three tabs on a company's workspace, and the platform's default notice from its own side.
- **Reports.** Acceptance status and cookie consent both download as Excel, with the evidence columns an audit asks for.
- The website's enquiry form records its own consent row against the notice version that was live, with the lead it created.

### The company website

- **A small site for each company**, generic for any industry — nothing in it is written for one trade. Sections: Design & colours, Pages & menu, SEO & sharing, Announcement bar; Hero banner, Story, What we do, Featured items, Offers, Testimonials, Gallery, Closing call-to-action; About us, Enquiry form, FAQ, Contact hours & social, Downloads, Footer & legal, Policies & consent.
- **The builder** is a list of sections with a switch on each and an editor beside it, exactly as the sections are defined in the registry — adding a section later needs one entry and no new screen. Sections the site cannot do without are marked **always** and have no switch.
- **The enquiry form creates a lead** through the same path every other channel uses, so de-duplication, routing and the campaign tag all behave as usual. A hidden field catches bots, and the form is rate-limited per address.
- The site is published or taken down from the builder, and lives at `<company address>/site`.

## Updates / Modifications

- `Company` gained `dpdpOfficer`, `dpdpOfficerEmail` and `site`. Three collections are new: `DpdpDocument` (main database), `DpdpConsent` and `CookieConsent` (each company's own).
- The **Activity Logs** screen is now **Logs**, with an Activity tab and a DPDP tab. The Activity tab is exactly what was there before.
- The company's Settings menu gains **DPDP**. Like every new module it starts switched off in each plan: tick **DPDP** on the plans that should have it (Super Admin › Plans), then it appears for those companies.
- Retention Policy will keep DPDP consents for ever by default — they are the evidence of consent and are not touched by the housekeeping job.

## Fixes

- The website's announcement bar used the brand colour as a plain CSS variable; the theme stores colours as RGB triplets, so the bar came out invisible. It now reads the variable correctly.

## Next

v1.5.0 — the Android and iOS apps, built by GitHub Actions and released from each company's S3 folder, with the Knowledge Base article for the build setup. v1.6.0 — in-app chat and push notices.

releases.title: The shared cache finds its own settings
releases.md:
## AS-IS

v1.3.0 and everything before it is unchanged. The company workspace, its twelve tabs, the per-company S3 layout and the stuck-menu fix all behave exactly as they were delivered.

## Fixes

- **The shared cache was silently off.** The platform only looked for `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` and `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`. A Redis store added from the Vercel marketplace is given different names — `KV_REST_API_URL` for Vercel KV, or a store-prefixed pair such as `REDIS_UPSTASH_LIGHTHOUSE_KV_REST_API_URL` — so the platform found nothing and every serverless instance kept its own copy of the cache. A change could then take a few seconds to show on another instance, and the same query was run once per instance. The pair is now found by itself: the hand-set names first, then Vercel KV's, then any `<STORE>_KV_REST_API_URL` with its matching token. A read-only token is ignored, because the cache has to write. Nothing needs renaming in Vercel.

## New Features

- **Super Admin › Settings › System Health shows the cache.** A card says whether it is On, how long a round trip takes and which variable it came from, and a banner appears when no store is configured at all — so this can never be wrong quietly again.

## Updates / Modifications

- `.env.example` now lists every variable the code reads, including all three accepted Redis pairs and the mobile-app build settings that v1.5.0 will use (`GITHUB_BUILD_REPO`, `GITHUB_BUILD_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_BUILD_REF`, `GITHUB_BUILD_WORKFLOW`, `MOBILE_BASE_VERSION`, `MOBILE_PACKAGE_PREFIX`, `MOBILE_IOS_SIGNING`). The Android and iOS signing keys are listed where they belong — in the build repository's GitHub secrets, never in the platform's environment.

Creating a company still uses the same pop-up.

## New Features

- **A company now opens as its own page.** Clicking a company’s name (or the pencil) in Super Admin › Company opens a full workspace at `/sa/companies/<id>` with a header — logo, status, plan, code, login e-mail, created date and address — and the actions that apply to the whole company: **Force login**, **Login page**, **Suspend / Activate** and **Save changes**. A new company is created in the same pop-up as before and then opens on its own page.
- **Overview** — this platform’s own figures for the company: leads in 7 days and in all, conversions, clients, outstanding (with upcoming shown separately), users and AI credits, live connectors, deliveries needing attention, open tickets, its three addresses with copy buttons, its users with last sign-in, its latest leads, and the current subscription cycle.
- **Company details** — legal name, business type, GSTIN, address, city, state, PIN, contact person, phone, WhatsApp, company e-mail, a separate contact e-mail and account status, beside the name, short name and code.
- **Subscription** — plan, payment frequency, amount, first due date, discount as ₹ **or** %, and the gross it works out to, with the current cycle shown underneath.
- **Login credentials** — owner name, WhatsApp, login e-mail and a new password with **Show** and **Generate**.
- **Branding & domain** — platform address and own domain, the company’s images, theme and accent colours, the 10 login designs with a live preview, the login page text, **login page colours** (headline, sub-headline, company name, tagline, “Sign in” title, form text, button and button text — each one Auto or a colour of its own) and **app themes** for the web and mobile apps. The S3 panel now lists what each area of the company’s folder holds.
- **White label** — hide platform branding, support link, e-mail sender name, app names for the web, mobile and admin apps, sidebar, corners and font, and custom CSS.
- **Role access** — the company’s own roles, edited by Super Admin, on the same grid the company sees. Everything is capped by the plan and by the Modules tab, so a paused module can never be granted. Saving a role here marks it as set by Super Admin.
- **Mobile Modules** — tick which modules and sub-modules this company’s mobile apps may use. The list is the platform’s own menu, so modules added later appear by themselves and start ticked.
- **Notifications** — every in-app notification with its own Mobile and Desktop switches and a sound, “apply one sound to all”, and **custom sounds** uploaded to the company’s own S3 folder.
- **Cron Jobs** — every background job with its schedule, last run and duration, next run, an on/off switch and **Run now**. A company can set its own interval or daily time for the jobs that work company by company; jobs that run once for the whole platform are marked **platform-wide** and can still be run for this company on demand.
- **Retention Policy** — how long each kind of log is kept, with its record count and oldest record, a per-row **Apply** and an **Apply now** for all. A new nightly housekeeping job (01:00 IST) deletes what is past its period. Logs that an audit may need have a floor and cannot be shortened below it.
- **Per-company S3 layout** — everything a company owns now sits under its own prefix: `branding/` (logo, banner, favicon, sounds), `app/` (mobile builds pushed by GitHub Actions), `brain/` (AI knowledge), `dpdp/` (consent documents) and `<Client Code>/<type>/` (attachments).

## Updates / Modifications

- **Editing a company moved out of the pop-up** onto the new page. The pop-up is still what creates a company, with the same four tabs; nothing was removed from it.
- `retry`, `billing` and `followups` now do their work company by company, each on that company’s own schedule, and record every run. The other jobs behave exactly as before and simply record their runs so the tab can show them.
- **Role Management inside the company** is unchanged. A role Super Admin saves is marked as set by Super Admin, which the company’s own screen shows.

## Fixes

- **A menu click that did not land.** After a deployment, a tab still running the old build cannot load the new code chunks; the route change was cancelled silently, the screen stayed where it was, and clicking another menu item did nothing until the page was reloaded by hand (the automatic stale-build reload is throttled to once in 30 seconds, which left the second and third click stranded). Every menu click is now watched: if the address has not changed a moment later, the browser is sent there directly, which fetches the new build and lands on the page that was clicked. The event is recorded in Activity Logs as a screen error, so a recurrence is visible.

## Next

v1.4.0 — DPDP consent (document upload or built-in editor, the scroll-to-the-end Accept screen, per-user acceptance, scrolling and cookie logs with downloadable reports) and the generic Website builder. v1.5.0 — the Android and iOS apps, built through GitHub Actions and released from each company’s S3 folder, with the Knowledge Base article for the build setup. v1.6.0 — in-app chat (one-to-one and groups) and push notices.

releases.title: Delete a client, verified by WhatsApp OTP
releases.md:
## AS-IS

Versions 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 continue unchanged except where listed below. No module, screen, field, permission or fix from an earlier version has been removed or altered — Sales Order grouping, Convert to Invoice with Discount and Gross, the Outstanding / Upcoming split, Company Name on leads, the rebuilt WhatsApp Logs, Integration › Needs attention, the compact UI and the Client Journey scroll area all behave exactly as in 1.1.0.

## New Features

- **Delete a client.** Client › Clients now has a delete action next to View journey on each row, verified by a one-time code on WhatsApp — the same gate Leads already use.
  - **Step 1 — what goes with it.** Before any code is sent, the dialog lists the client's footprint: sales order lines, unpaid invoices with their amount, pay-ins received with their amount, and support tickets with the open count. A reason can be recorded.
  - **Step 2 — OTP.** A 6-digit code is sent to the signed-in user's WhatsApp number (the company's number if the user has none) through the existing **Delete OTP** webhook event. Valid 5 minutes, 5 attempts.
  - **Step 3 — delete.** The client leaves Clients, the Service Board, Subscription Management and the client's support page. Its sales orders, invoices, pay-ins and tickets go with it, so no orphan rows are left behind in Sales Order, Invoice or Pay-In.
- **Nothing is erased.** A full snapshot — profile, journey, sales orders, invoices, pay-ins and tickets — is archived in the company's own database before the live rows are removed, together with who deleted it, when, and the reason given. The activity log records the same. Payment attachments in S3 are left untouched, so a deleted client can be reconstructed in full.
- **Delete is a permission, and it is never inherited.** Client › **Clients** now offers **Delete** in Role Management. Unlike every other sub-module action, it does **not** follow the Client module: a role has it only when the box on the **Clients** row is ticked, so no role that exists today silently gains the power to delete a client. The grid says so on the row. The company owner keeps full access as before, and Super Admin › Company › Modules can still restrict or pause it per company.

## Updates / Modifications

- The **Delete OTP** webhook event now covers both leads and clients; its description reads "One-time code to confirm deleting a lead or a client." The event key, template and any webhook already configured for it are unchanged and need no edit.
- A client that is deleted is never silently re-created: promotion of converted leads skips deleted records, and its recurring dues stop being generated.

## Fixes

- None outstanding from 1.1.0.

releases.title: Sales order grouping, lead company name, compact UI
releases.md:
## AS-IS

Version 1.0.0 continues unchanged except where listed below. No module, screen, field or permission has been removed.

## New Features

- **Convert to Invoice** on Sales Order. An icon on each client row (and on each service inside it) opens an invoice pre-filled with the client, services and amount, where a **Discount** can be entered as a fixed amount or a percentage — each one calculates the other — with **Gross** shown as payment amount minus discount.
- **Company Name on a lead.** A new field on Add / Edit lead and on the client, shown in the Leads list, searchable, included in import and export, and filled automatically from channels that send a company, business or organisation name.
- **Integration › Needs attention.** Any delivery from any channel that could not be saved as a lead is listed with its reason, with **Retry** and **Retry all**. Each keeps its original payload, so nothing is lost.
- **Release notes** at `/release`, with the version shown in the menu.

## Updates / Modifications

- **Sales Order now shows one row per client** with its services, licences and total. The row expands to the individual services, each keeping Edit, Delete and Reminder exactly as before.
- **Outstanding counts only what is due up to today.** Dues dated in future months are shown separately as **Upcoming**, on the client drawer and in the Clients list.
- **WhatsApp Logs** rebuilt: a Refresh button, the payload opening under its row instead of a pop-up, an `OK 200` result badge and the provider's own reply in Detail. Filters, Resend, retry status and pagination are unchanged.
- **Sample .xlsx / .csv** rebuilt to match the Add lead form, including Company Name, Service / product and No of Licenses, with a "How to fill" sheet. Files made from the older template still import.
- **Compact, professional UI** across the company screens: tighter tables, cards, forms and dialogs. Every section and field is retained.
- **Client Journey** now has its own scroll area inside the drawer, so the last entry is never cut off.
- **Faster screens**: menu, profile, service and picker data are served from the local cache at once and refreshed in the background, and survive a reload. A save still clears the cache, so nothing shown is stale.

## Fixes

- Stuck channel deliveries now retry 8 times with a widening gap (about 15 hours) instead of 5, and anything still stuck is visible and retryable instead of silently dead-lettered.
- Database indexes added for the outstanding split, grouped sales orders and the failed-delivery list.
